transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Hannah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Hannah, my email has completely stopped working on both my laptop Outlook and my iPad mail app since yesterday evening. It keeps popping up a box saying server disconnected or invalid credentials.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I would be glad to help resolve those email authentication errors and restore your email synchronization today, Yasmin. To begin, could you please confirm your first line of address and your four digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 18 Cambridge Gardens, London, W10 5UE, and my security PIN is three two seven zero.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Yasmin, that has verified your account on our Superfast Broadband and Mail hosting package. Let me open your mail server authentication logs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. I have been using this email address for over eight years without any issues until yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what is happening is that both your desktop Outlook client and your iPad mail application are unable to authenticate against our inbound and outbound mail servers, reporting connection dropped or credential errors. Have I got that right, Yasmin?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly! It prompts me for my password over and over again, and when I type it in, it just shakes and fails.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What is the exact email address you are trying to connect to?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The email address is yasmin dot mirza at s-net mail dot co dot uk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what port numbers are currently configured in your email client server settings?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have no idea about port numbers! I run a busy freelance accounting practice, and my small business clients are waiting on urgent quarterly VAT submissions that are due today! I cannot access their receipts or send the HMRC filing receipts, and I am completely overwhelmed with stress right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you open Outlook on your computer, click on File in the top left corner, and then select Account Settings?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First and foremost Yasmin, being locked out of your business email when client VAT deadlines and HMRC submissions are hanging in the balance is immensely stressful, and I am so sorry for that worry. We are going to step through this together calmly, and I will stay right with you until every email is sending and receiving smoothly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Hannah, that really helps. I was on the verge of tears ten minutes ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are in safe hands. As of yesterday evening, S-Net retired legacy unencrypted mail protocols to comply with modern telecommunications cybersecurity standards.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does retiring unencrypted protocols mean in plain English?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Older email settings used port 110 for POP3 and port 25 for SMTP without SSL encryption. We now require secure IMAP over port 993 with SSL/TLS, and secure SMTP over port 587 with STARTTLS.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, so my Outlook was still trying to talk to the old unencrypted door, and your servers locked it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an excellent analogy. In your Outlook Account Settings window, double-click on your S-Net mail profile to open the server settings.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Double clicking now... it has opened a window showing Incoming Mail Server and Outgoing Mail Server.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What does it say for the Incoming Mail Server hostname?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says mail dot s-net mail dot co dot uk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Change that to imap dot s-net dot net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing imap dot s-net dot net... done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And for the Outgoing Mail Server SMTP hostname, what does it show?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says smtp dot s-net mail dot co dot uk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Change that to smtp dot s-net dot net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Changed to smtp dot s-net dot net.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now click on More Settings in the bottom right corner, and select the Advanced tab.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking More Settings... Advanced tab... okay, I can see port numbers and encryption drop-down menus.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For Incoming Server IMAP, enter port 993, and in the drop-down box for encrypted connection, select SSL/TLS.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Port 993 entered, drop-down set to SSL/TLS.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: For Outgoing Server SMTP, enter port 587, and in the encryption drop-down, select STARTTLS.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Port 587 entered, encryption set to STARTTLS.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now switch to the Outgoing Server tab right next to Advanced. Is the checkbox for 'My outgoing server requires authentication' ticked?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, it was unticked! I have ticked it now, and selected 'Use same settings as my incoming mail server'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is vital, because modern SMTP servers reject outbound mail from unauthenticated clients to prevent spam relays.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood. That makes complete sense.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us address the password security requirement. To protect accounts against credential stuffing, S-Net now requires an App-Specific Password for desktop clients rather than your main portal password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do I generate an App-Specific Password?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open a web browser on your computer and navigate to webmail dot s-net dot net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Navigating to webmail dot s-net dot net... logging in with my main password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on the gear icon in the top right for Settings, then select Security, and click Generate App Password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Settings... Security... Generate App Password. It's asking for a device name.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Type 'Work Outlook' as the device label and click Generate.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It generated a sixteen-character code: w x k p - m r t q - z b c d - v n l s.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what was that primary S-Net mail address again, Yasmin?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's yasmin dot mirza at s-net mail dot co dot uk, like I told you at the start of the call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Copy that sixteen-character app password and paste it into the Outlook password box, then click Next to run the test.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pasting into the Outlook box... clicking Next... it's running the test... 'Log on to incoming mail server: Completed'! 'Send test email message: Completed'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Both green ticks on incoming and outgoing! That confirms Outlook is communicating over TLS 1.3.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My inbox just populated with forty unread client emails! That is fantastic!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us configure your iPad so your mobile access is equally synchronized.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, let's fix the iPad now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On your iPad, open Settings, scroll down to Mail, tap Accounts, and tap on your S-Net account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Settings... Mail... Accounts... S-Net. Found it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tap on Account Settings at the top to view the server fields.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening Account Settings... yes, incoming and outgoing hostnames are displayed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Update the Incoming Host Name to imap dot s-net dot net, and the Outgoing Host Name to smtp dot s-net dot net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Updating hostnames to imap dot s-net dot net and smtp dot s-net dot net. Done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tap on Outgoing Mail Server SMTP, then tap Primary Server. Is Use SSL enabled, and is Server Port set to 587?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Use SSL was on, but port was set to 25. I have changed Server Port to 587.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now tap Done, go back to Advanced, ensure Use SSL is enabled under Incoming Settings, and set Server Port to 993.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Under Advanced... Use SSL is on, server port changed from 143 to 993.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now we need a second unique App-Specific Password for the iPad. In your webmail browser window, click Generate Another App Password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Generating another app password... naming it 'iPad Accounting'... clicking Generate.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What code did the system generate?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It generated: f j q r - b t v w - x z y k - m p h c.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Type that code into the Password field on your iPad.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing it into the iPad password box now... tapping Done... it says 'Verifying' with a spinning wheel.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It popped up an error saying 'Cannot Get Mail - The user name or password for imap dot s-net dot net is incorrect'! I have typed this ridiculous code in twice now, and it keeps rejecting it! I am so exhausted and stressed, Hannah! I have three client VAT submissions due before midnight, and now my iPad is throwing errors! Why does everything have to be so difficult?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tap on the Password field on your iPad, delete all characters, and check if the very first letter capitalized itself.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Typing long complex security codes on a glass tablet screen when you are rushing against a midnight VAT deadline is completely exhausting and stressful, Yasmin, and I completely understand why you are feeling so frustrated. Take a deep breath, we are almost at the finish line, and I will make sure this iPad connects.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Hannah. You're right, I just looked, and the iPad automatically capitalized the 'F' into a capital F because it thought it was the start of a sentence!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Apple iOS keyboards default to auto-capitalization. Make sure the 'f' is entered in lowercase: f j q r - b t v w - x z y k - m p h c without spaces.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing it carefully in all lowercase... tapping Done... spinning wheel... all blue checkmarks appeared!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Blue checkmarks on iOS confirm complete TLS authentication with the IMAP server.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening the Mail app on my iPad... all my folders and forty emails just synchronized right in front of my eyes!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us send a test email from your iPad to yourself to verify outbound SMTP relay.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Composing test message to myself... tapping send... whoosh sound effect... and it immediately pinged into Outlook on my laptop!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Both your desktop Outlook and your mobile iPad are fully synchronized with modern TLS 1.3 encryption and dedicated app passwords.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have no idea what a relief this is. I can submit all three client VAT returns before eight o'clock tonight now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does that completely resolve your email connection and authentication issues today, Yasmin?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, completely and totally resolved. You've been so patient and wonderful, Hannah.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my absolute pleasure assisting you. Is there anything else on your S-Net account I can help with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's everything. Thank you so much again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for contacting S-Net technical help, take care Yasmin. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
